target_customer: Biotechs, pharma companies and CROs preparing IND submissions for first-in-human trials
problem: Biotechs spend months stitching together reports from contractors and internal teams to assemble an IND submission. Scoop drafts modules from study reports, CMC data and protocols and checks consistency across the dossier.
business_model: B2B SaaS for regulatory submission drafting (pricing not public)
product_category: AI regulatory document automation for life sciences

founders.name: Vincent Park
founders.background_notes: YC page: led AI document processing for Fortune 10 customers at Persona, earlier tech lead at Dropbox. Education not listed. Says the founders met at UPenn.

founders.name: Jay Kwon
education: University of Pennsylvania, MS Computer Science
founders.background_notes: YC page: supported IND filings and Phase III trial design for an ALS therapy at Corestem.

competitors.name: Weave Bio
competitors.what: AI platform (AutoIND) to draft and review regulatory documents including INDs
competitors.traction_then: Launched its platform publicly in May 2024; claims a first IND draft in a day (vendor claim)

technical_complexity.rationale: Document drafting with cited sources and cross-document consistency checks over eCTD-style dossiers is standard LLM engineering with hard parts around traceability and accuracy, buildable by two founders with Gemini-era tooling.

defensibility.rationale: Weave Bio already sold a similar product in 2024, the founders' domain depth is a plus, but drafting workflows are copyable and there is no named customer or data asset yet.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not yet observable; the company is months old at the time of research.

market_need_then: The YC description says biotechs spend months consolidating contractor and internal reports to file an IND. A December 2025 industry guide notes sponsors remain responsible for what they file, so AI is positioned as drafting support.

branding.domain_note: Uses scooplabs.ai, not scoop.com or scoop.ai; contact is founders@scooplabs.ai.

identity.logo: Not described in any source found
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, direct and practical; short declarative headlines such as 'Submit INDs in days, not months' and 'Every sentence cited'.

brand_strength.rationale: A very new company with no press about the brand; the name collides with several unrelated companies called Scoop (Scoop Analytics, Scoop News, Scoop Technologies) in search results.

outcome_analysis: Scoop is an active Fall 2025 company with two founders, one of whom has direct IND and clinical trial experience from Corestem and Genentech. No acquisition, shutdown or layoff news exists. Weave Bio had already launched a competing IND drafting product in 2024, so the open question is whether source-cited drafting wins customers against it. Funding is not public beyond the YC deal.
notes: VCBacked lists about $500K pre-seed in Nov 2025 with Y Combinator as investor; seen only on aggregators and matching the standard YC deal, so it is unverified and not recorded as a round. A Caplight $16M Series A headline belongs to a different company. No outcome news found beyond YC and aggregator pages. Ritivel (YC) is a similar company but no dated source was found, so it is not listed as a competitor at founding.
